notes: Read all three units, all eleven candidates and the review. Removed the nonpolicy meeting introduction. Resolved the causal allegation as Democrats in power responding to Trump's actions only because those actions targeted other capitalist-class figures, especially Joe Biden. Preserved attempts rather than completed actions for caging, visa denial and the public-charge rule, corrected the Democratic-establishment predicate, and restored the omitted imperative for socialists to combine candidate support, a positive vision and resistance to establishment appropriation or dilution.

claims.claim_text: Democrats in power responded to President Trump's actions only because those actions sought to affect other members of the capitalist class, particularly presumed 2020 Democratic front-runner Joe Biden.
Socialists must balance support for elected candidates with articulating a positive vision of the world they seek to build.
Socialists should welcome establishment hostility from actors seeking to claim credit for socialist work while diluting it beyond recognition.
The Trump administration attempted to cage immigrant children and families as part of its worsening of the existing immigration system.
The Trump administration attempted to deny visas to immigrants without health care as part of its worsening of the existing immigration system.
The Trump administration attempted to uphold a public-charge rule for immigrants in need as part of its worsening of the existing immigration system.
The Trump administration's listed immigration actions were insufficient to prompt the Democratic establishment to fight for immigrant communities.
